newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end up, helped by Fed.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end up, helped by Fed.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Tuesday, continuing this week's shortcovering rally, helped near the close by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision not to raise interest rates.

"After falling for three weeks, a bounce was expected from oversold levels anyway this week, but the market had probably already discounted a Fed rate hike and saw some shortcovering when the Fed failed to move," California-based Imperial Bank's chief bullion dealer, Jeff Singer said.
"Longer term though the outlook is probably still bearish for precious metals without much inflation on the horizon."
"The shortcovering rally is probably nearly done, but with large short positions now built up it's possible more profit taking could be seen," he said.
COMEX gold ended up $1.30 an ounce at $385.70 an ounce, after trading in a $384.40-385.80 range on total gold futures estimated volume of 27,000 lots.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted $382.60/383.10, compared to the London afternoon fix at $382.30 and the New York close Monday at $381.50-382.00.
COMEX silver ended up 4.0 cents at $4.935 an ounce, after trading in a $4.880-4.940 range.

Commodity price indices weakened in the past month, despite the surge in oil prices, suggesting there is little immediate inflationary threat to the U.S. economy, and little reason to buy precious metals as an inflation hedge, analysts said.

"While the U.S. labor market is tight, unless and until the leading non-employment indicators of inflation concur with the employment indicators, inflation is unlikely to break out of its current (2.0-3.5 pct annual) range," the Economic Cycle Research Institute's New York based co-director, Anirvan Banerji, said.

NYMEX October platinum ended up $1.30 an ounce at $390.20 and NYMEX December palladium ended up 15 cents at $119.00, after fixing at a fresh two and a half year low in London in the bullion market Monday.
